title: MCP server crashes on the notifications/initialized notification — handshake never completes
evidence: BrazilianSoccerMcpServer.java:7 — the main read-loop catch block builds Map.of("jsonrpc","2.0","error",...,"id",null); java.util.Map.of rejects null values. notifications/initialized hits the switch default in response() (line 8) and throws IllegalArgumentException, which reaches that catch and NPEs. Reproduced by stdio probe: initialize answered, then `Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NullPointerException at java.util.Map.of(Map.java:1410) <- main(BrazilianSoccerMcpServer.java:7)`, process exits 1, tools/list left unanswered. Independently corroborated by _factual.json score=0.0 'did not complete the MCP handshake'.
suggestion: Reply to JSON-RPC notifications (requests with no id) with nothing, and build error/response objects with a null-tolerant map (HashMap) so a null id does not throw.

title: Server process dies on any error input (unknown method/tool, missing required arg) instead of returning a JSON-RPC error
evidence: response() default (line 8) and call() default (line 9) throw IllegalArgumentException; required() (line 12) throws on missing args. Every throw reaches the same main catch at line 7 whose Map.of(...,"id",null) NPEs. Reproduced in three separate processes — bogus/method, tools/call name=no_such_tool, and team_statistics with empty arguments — each exits 1 at Map.of(Map.java:1410); a valid team_statistics{team:Flamengo} call by contrast returns correctly, confirming only the error path crashes.
suggestion: Construct the JSON-RPC error with a null-tolerant map, echo the request id, and keep the read loop alive after catching a per-request error.

title: JSON-RPC response id serialized as float (1.0) rather than integer (1)
evidence: Probe responses come back as {"id":1.0,...} for integer request id 1 — Json.parse stores numbers as doubles, so the echoed id type deviates from the request. Minor JSON-RPC spec deviation, non-fatal.
suggestion: Preserve integral ids as integers when echoing them back.
